_about:
WHICH STEPS MATTER FIRST - a sidecar, for the same reason steps.tanglish.json is one.

CLAUDE.md open item 8: a new project opens on step 01 of 32 with nothing
saying which of them are load-bearing and which can wait. This file is the
answer, and it is DATA rather than a list in code because a hand-written
list of the steps is wrong by the second change - invariant 2.

WHY A SIDECAR. src/data/steps.feature.json and steps.short.json are
REGENERATED by `npm run extract` from legacy/, so a `spine: true` written
into a step there is destroyed by the next extraction and legacy/ must never
be edited to stop that. steps.production.json is hand-written and would
survive - but splitting the same fact across two files by whether the file
happens to be generated is how the two halves drift. One file, all
namespaces. src/ui/steps.js merges it at render time.

Keyed `<namespace>:<step id>`, exactly like the Tanglish sidecar, because
step ids repeat across blueprints - there is a step-01 in both the feature
and the short.

WHAT NOTHING HERE DOES. It removes nothing and hides nothing by default.
The completionist still has all 32 steps in the order they have always been
in; the spine is an ordering of IMPORTANCE laid over the ordering of TIME,
and the filter that narrows the page to it is off until somebody asks for it.

THE SPINE is the shortest path to a blueprint you could actually show
somebody. It is not a guess: nine of the ten steps below are the ones the
pitch deck on this page reads to build its slides, and the tenth (the scene
list) is the one the rest of the studio reads. Order is the order to do them
in, and it is the array order - nothing here carries a rank number, because
a rank number and an array order are two representations of one thing.

UNLOCKS names a thing IN THIS APP that reads the step's answers. Every entry
was checked against the code that consumes it (buildPitchSlides, renderCharMap,
renderPacingChart, renderSceneChart, updateBudget, updateVol1Bridge,
exportMarkdown in src/pages/feature.js). If you add one, check it the same way
- an unlock nobody honours is worse than none, because it is a promise.

spine.note: The one question the film is. Everything below is an answer to it.
One sentence. Until it exists you cannot tell anyone what you are making.
What the film argues, and what it wagers on the argument.
Who changes. Name, want, need, wound, arc — five lines, and the film has a spine.
The opposing want. A protagonist with nothing pushing back is a description, not a story.
Era, place, rules. The third character, and the one the budget is really about.
Fifteen beats. The first point at which the whole film exists in one place.
The scene list. Everything downstream of the blueprint — breakdown, board, schedule — starts here.
One page every department reads. Without it the crew are making different films.
Days, money, heads of department. The three numbers a producer asks for first.
